ev.quote: https://rowanzellers.com/hellaswag

contribution.value: HellaSwag is a 70k-question commonsense NLI benchmark built via Adversarial Filtering (AF) with GPT generations and BERT discriminators; it is easy for humans (>95%) but hard for state-of-the-art models (<48%).

ev.quote: we show that commonsense inference still proves difficult for even stateof-the-art models, by presenting HellaSwag. a new challenge dataset. Though its questions are trivial for humans (>95\% accuracy), state-of-the-art models struggle (<48%).

We use Adversarial Filtering (AF), a data-collection paradigm in which a series of discriminators is used to select a challenging set of generated wrong answers. AF is surprisingly effective towards this goal: the resulting dataset of 70k problems is easy for humans (95.6% accuracy), yet challenging for machines (<50%).
We start by including video captions from the ActivityNet Captions dataset (Krishna et al., 2017).
We next consider a new and challenging testbed for commonsense reasoning: completing how-to articles from WikiHow, an online how-to manual. We scrape 80k context and follow-up paragraphs from WikiHow
SWAG is a dataset for commonsense NLI. For each question, a model is given a **context** from a video caption and four **ending choices** for what might happen next.

data_size.value: 70k problems total: 25k ActivityNet contexts and 45k WikiHow contexts; 10K validation and 10K test (5k in-domain + 5k zero-shot each).

ev.quote: we craft two subsets: one containing 5k 'in-domain' examples that come from categories as seen during training (Figure [8)](#page-5-0), and another with 5k 'zero-shot' examples from randomly chosen held-out categories. In total, there are 70k dataset examples.
Table 1: Performance of models, evaluated with accuracy (%).We report results on the full validation and test sets (Overall), as well as results on informative subsets of the data

key_results.value: BERT-Large reaches 47.3% test accuracy on HellaSwag overall vs 95.6% human accuracy (gap > 48%)
BERT-Large drops from 86% on SWAG to 47.3% on HellaSwag, while ESIM+ELMo drops from 59% (SWAG) to 33.3% (HellaSwag)

ev.quote: while ESIM+ELMo obtained 59% accuracy on SWAG, it obtains only 33.3% accuracy on HellaSwag.

key_results.value: BERT-Large zero-shot test accuracy 45.0% vs in-domain 49.7%, a 4.7-point drop on novel categories

ev.quote: egories. Performance drops roughly 5% on the test fold, which suggests that the finetuning is not enough for BERT to learn to generalize to novel activities or how-to categories.

key_results.value: BERT-Large transfers poorly: trained on SWAG, evaluated on HellaSwag scores only 34.6%; SWAG models on WikiHow get just 28%

ev.quote: Figure 9: Transfer experiments from SWAG to Hella-Swag and vice versa, evaluated on the validation sets. Overall, a BERT-Large that is trained on SWAG hardly generalizes to HellaSwag: it scores 34.6%.

ev.section: 6.1 How easy might HellaSwag be for future discriminators?
ev.quote: Figure 12: Estimated pretraining hours required to reach a desired accuracy on HellaSwag. We estimate perfomance with respect to a RTX 2080 Ti - a modern, fast GPU

strengths.value: Builds a 70k commonsense NLI benchmark that is trivial for humans (>95%) yet hard for state-of-the-art models (<50%).

ev.quote: the resulting dataset of 70k problems is easy for humans (95.6% accuracy), yet challenging for machines (<50%).

strengths.value: Identifies a Goldilocks zone of generation length where outputs fool BERT yet humans easily reject them.

ev.quote: Our investigation reveals a Goldilocks zone – roughly three sentences of context, and two generated sentences – wherein generations are largely nonsensical, even though state-of-the-art discriminators cannot reliably tell the difference

strengths.value: Includes a zero-shot evaluation split using held-out categories to measure generalization beyond seen domains.

ev.quote: another with 5k 'zero-shot' examples from randomly chosen held-out categories. In total, there are 70k dataset examples.

strengths.value: Releases dataset and code publicly for community use.

ev.section: 6.1 How easy might HellaSwag be for future discriminators?
ev.quote: Answering this question is challenging because *these models don't exist (or are unavailable) at* *the time of writing*.

weaknesses.value: Compute extrapolation to human-level (10^9 GPU-hours) is a rough Roofline estimate, not a measurement.

ev.quote: This estimation is a rough estimate: we convert reported TPU runtimes to our benchmark RTX 2080 Ti GPU using the Roofline model

weaknesses.value: Acknowledges that future models may solve HellaSwag by picking up on spurious patterns rather than reasoning.

ev.quote: future models might answer correctly only by picking up on spurious patterns, in which case a new development of the benchmark – using these models as adversaries – would place us in the same position as we are right now.

limitations.value: Covers only English text from ActivityNet captions and WikiHow articles; no multilingual or other domains.

ev.quote: We scrape 80k context and follow-up paragraphs from WikiHow, covering such diverse topics as "how to make an origami owl" to "how to survive a bank robbery."

limitations.value: Benchmark is static; once solved, requires a new dataset crowdsourced via the same process.

ev.section: 6.3 Towards a future of evolving benchmarks
ev.quote: What happens when HellaSwag gets solved? We believe the answer is simple: crowdsource another dataset, with the same exact format, and see where models fail.

limitations.value: Does not evaluate model robustness under quantization, compression, or any post-training modification.
Does not report compute, energy, or per-token latency for any of the evaluated models.

future_work_stated.value: Crowdsource a new dataset in the same format once HellaSwag is solved, using future state-of-the-art models as adversaries.

ev.section: 6.3 Towards a future of evolving benchmarks
ev.quote: What happens when HellaSwag gets solved? We believe the answer is simple: crowdsource another dataset, with the same exact format, and see where models fail.

future_work_stated.value: Move benchmarks toward an adversarial co-evolution loop with state-of-the-art generators and discriminators.

ev.quote: we provided insight into the inner workings of pretrained models, and suggest a path for NLP progress going forward: towards benchmarks that adversarially co-evolve with evolving state-of-the-art models.
Short for Harder Endings, Longer contexts, and Low-shot Activities for Situations With Adversarial Generations. Dataset and code at https://rowanzellers.com/hellaswag.
